project_type: Flask backend + vanilla JavaScript frontend; ML pipeline (PyMuPDF, sentence-transformers, OpenAI/Gemini) for policy comparison
build_system: pip-based; no build step. Virtual environment at d:\jig\venv
test_framework: pytest; tests at ml_pipeline/tests/ and root-level test files
verification_instructions: 1. Run pytest to verify no regressions. 2. Start Flask dev server: python frontend/app.py. 3. Open http://localhost:5000 and test investigation flow manually. 4. Verify two-PDF comparison still works unchanged.
environment_constraints: Flask dev server runs on localhost:5000 with auto-browser open. API keys (GEMINI_API_KEY, GROQ_API_KEY) read from environment via python-dotenv. Never hardcode keys. Search API keys (SERPER_API_KEY, BRAVE_API_KEY) will be added to .env pattern.
contribution_requirements: No AGENTS.md or CONTRIBUTING.md found; follow existing patterns. Keep API keys in environment variables. Do not break existing /compare endpoint. Do not modify ML pipeline comparison logic. Keep investigation logic separate from core pipeline.
key_patterns: Flask routes use @app.route decorator; frontend/app.py has /compare and /sample endpoints. Frontend is vanilla JS with fetch API; index.html has single-file structure. ML pipeline uses Pydantic v2 models (ml_pipeline/models.py) for all data structures. Config loaded via ml_pipeline/config.py load_config() from environment. Tests use conftest.py fixtures (make_clause, make_pdf_bytes, sample_clause_a/b).
directory_structure: d:\jig (root): frontend/ (Flask app + templates + static), ml_pipeline/ (extractor, segmenter, aligner, detector, summarizer, citations, pipeline, models, config, tests/), sample_policies/ (Greenfield sample PDFs), venv/ (virtual environment), requirements.txt, conftest.py (pytest root config)
